title: Keep a marker from rewarding length
statement: Model judges favour longer answers and one position, so length-normalise a marker's inputs, swap the order of compared answers, and test it on short full-credit answers.
detail: An assessment BrainLift, citing published work on model judges, says they show first-or-second position effects and favour more verbose responses, and names randomised sides, length-normalised inputs and repeated, permuted comparisons as the mitigations. A grade 4-5 writing module's marker spec adopts length-normalising and side-swapping of anchor order even in absolute scoring, since longer answers would otherwise inflate, and its generation contract requires a short full-credit and a long partial-credit answer among the exemplars so that longest does not count as best.

evidence.quote: LLM judges show left/right (or first/second) position effects and favour more verbose responses; mitigate via randomised sides, length-normalised inputs, and repeated, permuted comparisons.
Audit: track judge agreement with human seeds; estimate reliability; check for systemic biases (position, verbosity).
**length-normalise** inputs and **side-swap** anchor order even in absolute scoring, or longer Grade-4 answers inflate.
**A correct 2 can be short**: do not let "longest = best" (`[WF 1963]`); the exemplar set must include a short full-credit and a long partial-credit response.

citations.ref: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena (arXiv:2306.05685, NeurIPS 2023)
